title: Rio Grande Buoys Break Loose Again, Raising Water Supply Concerns at City Council
excerpt: About 12 buoys in the Rio Grande came loose during recent flooding and were recovered on the Mexican side of the river, Mayor Victor Treviño told the Laredo City Council on Monday, raising fresh concerns about risks to the city's drinking water supply, according to KGNS.
content:
About 12 buoys in the Rio Grande came loose during recent flooding and were recovered on the Mexican side of the river, Laredo Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño told the Laredo City Council on Monday, according to KGNS.

The mayor's update to the council raised fresh concerns about potential risks to the area's water supply, the station reported. The Rio Grande is Laredo's only source of drinking water, and the mayor has said river structures could interfere with water intakes, especially when water levels rise.

It is the second time since July flooding that buoys in the river near Webb County have come loose after heavy rainfall, KGNS reported earlier this month. KGNS cameras captured loose buoys in the river following the rainfall, and the mayor said they landed on the Mexican side, where water intakes are more exposed.

Treviño has called for the buoys to be recovered and for a pause on further placement until the federal government provides a full study of how the buoys are anchored and what risks they pose if they break loose. The city has not received such a study, he said.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed to KGNS that buoys became dislodged, that they were under a contractor's control and that deployment efforts have restarted. The agency told KGNS it has placed 14 miles of a planned 122 miles of waterborne barriers in the Laredo sector.

The city has not reported that the latest incident contaminated its water supply. Treviño has said loose buoys could create debris, affect the river's flow or wash onto the Mexican side, and that officials in Nuevo Laredo are asking why the barriers are ending up there.

Residents of the Azteca neighborhood also raised concerns about the possibility of a border wall being built through their community, KGNS reported. Mayor Treviño said Laredo has avoided a border wall through negotiation and collaboration, and that he plans to keep presenting evidence to officials to prevent wall construction in the Azteca area.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 11, 2026.
